title: The Orchard of Vilna
premise: In 1940 Vilna, Juniper Amberdale, a half-Jewish apprentice clockmaker raised by the gentile Amberdales, is summoned to repair the university observatory's master clock and finds a sealed letter hidden in its case: proof that a Lithuanian collaborator official plans to seize the property and lives of the very family that took him in. As occupation orders tighten, Juniper must move the letter past three checkpoints to a resistance printer before the family's deportation date. He succeeds at terrible cost—his mentor dies covering his escape—but the printed evidence forces an officer's exposure, and Juniper, no longer invisible, claims his place as both heir and witness.
about_author: Bram Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rescued documents from occupied Lithuania. The Orchard of Vilna is his first novel, drawn from the marginalia of confiscated letters he was never supposed to read.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the Amberdale clock shop, Juniper measures his life in tolerances—invisible as an apprentice, loved but never quite claimed. A summons arrives for him alone to repair the observatory master clock. Emotional beat: quiet longing for belonging, shadowed by the first rumors of new occupation decrees.

chapters.title: What the Clock Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Inside the observatory housing he finds a sealed letter tucked behind the escapement—a denunciation naming the Amberdales for seizure and deportation, signed by official Kazys Radvila. Terrified, he reassembles the clock and pockets the letter. Emotional beat: vertigo; the moment invisibility becomes impossible.

chapters.title: Supper with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Juniper and Marta Amberdale, his adoptive mother. Over dinner, Marta hints she has always known what Juniper is and what's coming, while he conceals the letter. Emotional beat: found family strained by protective silence; love expressed through things unsaid.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Carrying the letter sewn into his tool roll, Juniper crosses the Green Bridge checkpoint, aided by a sympathetic guard who once bought a watch from his mentor. But he realizes Radvila suspects the letter is missing. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Lessons in Corruption
chapters.summary: Radvila's POV. The collaborator official interrogates the observatory keeper, tightens the checkpoints, and reveals his own debts and ambitions—the machinery of a small man grown monstrous. Emotional beat: chilling intimacy with banal evil; power feeding on fear.

chapters.title: The Printer on Pylimo Street
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper seeks the resistance printer, an old schoolteacher named Feiga, who agrees to reproduce the letter but needs three days—and demands Juniper return to help distribute it. Emotional beat: reluctant recruitment; found family expanding beyond blood.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Brass
chapters.summary: Mentor Tobias's POV. Radvila's men trace the summons to the shop. Tobias, Juniper's teacher, sends Juniper away with the letter and a repaired pocket watch, then stays behind to stall them. Emotional beat: sacrificial inheritance—the craft passed on at the cost of a life.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Grieving and hunted, Juniper attempts the rail yard crossing with forged papers from Feiga's network. A young guard recognizes the pocket watch as Tobias's work and lets him pass—or so Juniper believes until he hears boots behind him. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into urgency; trust as a gamble.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climax. Cornered at the third checkpoint near the old family orchard, Juniper is saved when Marta appears, claiming him publicly as her son before the guards—an act that marks her too. The letter reaches Feiga's press as sirens rise. Emotional beat: the found family made visible and unbreakable at the moment of greatest danger.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the printed letter circulates; Radvila is exposed and removed by his own superiors. The Amberdales' deportation is stayed, though the war grinds on. Juniper winds the observatory clock, now apprenticed to memory as much as mechanism. Emotional beat: bittersweet inheritance—he keeps time for those who kept him.
